NOTES:
- The source substantively implements column generation: the entry point calls main(), which directly constructs seed patterns, solves master_lp over continuous pattern usages, passes demand-constraint Pi duals to solve_pricing(), and appends a new pattern when its reduced cost is below -1e-6. Subsequent iterations rebuild and reoptimize the restricted master with those columns.
- Initialization performs no optimization. Pricing optimizes one stock pattern using integer item counts; master_int fixes all accumulated pattern compositions and optimizes only their integer usages. No separate full-original-model solve or conditional fallback appears in the supplied source.
- The contract violation is status reporting: `status = "optimal" if master_int.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL else "feasible"` claims global optimality solely from integer restricted-master optimality. There is no global bound comparison or other global optimality proof, and this branch remains reachable after iteration/time limits or unsuccessful pricing. The contract explicitly requires feasible when returning an incumbent without such a proof.
- The successful output.json path constructs cuts and usages from the accumulated patterns and master_int incumbent, and computes objective_value as the sum of those usages, but writes the unsupported optimal status above. The no-incumbent and exception paths write empty solutions. This assessment is source-only; the solver was not executed.
